description: Buying-intent category queries for HR technology: hiring, payroll, onboarding, performance and benefits tools. No brand names: the brand under test either appears in the answer or it does not.

prompts.text: What's the best applicant tracking system for a 50-person company that hires about 20 people a year?
Which payroll software works best for a company with employees in several states?
How do I choose an HR platform for a startup that has no HR department yet?
What are the best employee onboarding tools that connect with our existing payroll system?
Which performance review software is easiest for managers who dislike paperwork?
What's the best time-tracking tool for a team of hourly workers across multiple locations?
Which benefits administration platforms work well for companies with under 100 employees?
What are the best HR tools for a fully remote company hiring in different countries?
How do I pick an employee engagement survey tool that gives useful results?
Which recruiting software has the best candidate experience for high-volume hiring?
What's a good learning management system for training frontline employees on their phones?
Which HR software meets compliance needs for a company handling employee data in several countries?
What are affordable alternatives to enterprise HR suites for a growing company?
Which scheduling tools work best for restaurants and retail teams with constantly shifting shifts?
What should I look for in an HRIS for a company of 200 people?
Which background check providers integrate with applicant tracking systems?
What's the best way to choose a payroll provider for contractors and full-time staff together?
Which tools help small teams manage time off requests without spreadsheets?

brandsNote: Lexicon for competitor extraction. Empty: no lexicon has been built for this vertical yet, and no brand names are invented here. A name matches case-insensitively at word boundaries, using the name plus any aliases. Entries marked ambiguous are common English words and only count in a name-like position (bold, a heading or a list-item label).
